title: Per-model Performance Snapshot Cards: compact metric cards for routes and models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact, scannable set of performance snapshot cards that appear on model and route list views and on detailed route pages. Each card surfaces latency distribution, throughput trend, token breakdown, and an actionable cost signal so engineers and product owners can quickly triage performance regressions and capacity decisions.
design_rationale: Users need a fast, scannable summary when inspecting many routes/models — full charts are still available on drill-in but list-level context reduces discovery time and noisy paging into detail views.
Prioritize p95 and p50 for latency, 1m and 5m throughput trends, and token-level cost so teams can connect behavior with unit economics without running custom queries.
Cards must be layout-agnostic (grid or list), responsive, and use a single-color-per-metric palette to avoid visual noise in dense tables.
Support small multipliers (sparklines) and an expandable pane for micro-traces when a user needs deeper context.
Design for accessibility: color contrast, descriptive aria labels, and fractionally large tap targets for mobile/compact console usage.
proposed_charts: Latency band ribbon: stacked bands for p50/p90/p95 with distribution shade and a small numeric badge for current p95 (ms)
Throughput micro-sparkline: 1h/24h toggle with min/avg/max hover and a tiny numeric for current rps
Token flow mini Sankey: percent split of prompt vs completion tokens (compact two-node flow) and estimated cost-per-call
Error & fallback indicator: icon + short text showing error-rate change vs baseline (1h/24h)
Cost-per-token heat strip: single-row color bar representing median cost-per-1k tokens across last 24h
acceptance_criteria: Card appears in model/route list and on top of route detail page as a condensed header widget
Latency ribbon displays p50/p90/p95 and aligns with runtime telemetry mapping (units in ms)
Throughput sparkline supports hover tooltip and 1h/24h toggles; values match backend /metrics API within 2%
Token flow shows prompt/completion % and calculates estimated call cost using active pricing profile
Clickable card expands to reveal 3-panel micro-traces (latency histogram, token waterfall, recent errors) with links to full performance canvas
Design assets provided in Figma with tokens and ready CSS vars; accessible color tokens included
engineering_notes: Backend must expose aggregated p50/p90/p95 and token splits via /api/v1/metrics/snapshots to avoid client-side heavy queries
Suggest a single JSON payload per page to drive all cards (batch requests) for performance on list views
Rendering should use canvas-sparkline for 1px crispness in high-density tables; fallback to SVG for older browsers
Expose 'cost_estimate' computed by pricing service so UI doesn't re-calc with inconsistent rates
accessibility_checks: Contrast ratio 4.5:1 for numeric badges on colored backgrounds
Keyboard navigation to expand/collapse cards and open micro-traces
Screen-reader labels for each metric with short summary sentence, e.g., 'Route X: p95 latency 120ms, throughput 4 rps, prompt 70% of tokens'
risks_and_tradeoffs: Adding cards to list views may increase initial page payload — mitigated by lazy-loading the token flow mini-sankey on hover
Compact visualization trades detail for scanability; include direct links to full canvas for deep dives
Multiple metric computations (p95, cost-per-token) may be expensive if computed ad-hoc — prefer aggregated pre-computation in the metrics pipeline
